title: Reduce complexity
why: A function exceeds configured complexity thresholds.
suggestion: Split or simplify the function, or document a local suppression when one cohesive parser or traversal must retain shared state.
limitations: JavaScript and TypeScript extraction covers named declarations, methods, and block-bodied variable arrow functions.
Anonymous callbacks and expression-bodied arrow functions are not measured.
Cyclomatic complexity counts each logical operator, while cognitive complexity counts a consecutive chain of the same logical operator once.
Complex localization implementations are grouped into one repository finding with related locations.
Python comments and single-line or triple-quoted string contents are excluded from complexity signals.
Rust complexity measurement excludes nested named callable bodies and local impl declarations from their enclosing function without changing extracted sources or locations.
Recognized empty Rust closure delimiters are not boolean OR operators; executable branches inside closures and ordinary runtime macros remain part of their enclosing function.

Rust quote-crate quote! token templates are excluded when a direct qualified call or an explicit direct/grouped import establishes the macro binding; simple imported aliases are supported and local macro_rules shadowing is retained conservatively.
Unresolved or re-exported quote aliases, wildcard imports, quote_spanned! and other macros are retained; macro expansion and full Rust name resolution are not performed.

Rust callable boundaries are lexical; inline declarations not recognized by extraction may not be separated. Cognitive nesting remains a brace-depth approximation that includes ordinary scopes, match arms and closures.
